lead: you drove the whole length of it with her — every appointment, the bad autumn, the flat with no heating — and a man you talked to for ten minutes once runs a business you have never heard of.
sun: the going-with is the half of you that has witnesses. you are in the car, in the waiting rooms, on the phone at eleven at night, for as long as it takes, and it ends at a door you do not go through. that half of your life has names and dates in it and could be listed. every item on the list is somebody else's arrival, and you were the transport.
moon: the other half throws things into people and loses them the same hour — a sentence, a name — and they grow into somebody's decade under another name. your moon is the turning point of that road: set out from your sun in either direction and this is where the walk out becomes the walk back, and nothing you did could put it further off.
pull: the record of you is four arrivals and one road you turned round on. everything else you ever set going is out there under names you would not recognise.
tension: asked what you have actually done, you can produce four names. saying them out loud puts your name across four lives that were lived by somebody else, so you do not, and what comes out instead is a shrug. the other half cannot be produced at all — it left your hands without registering and is now furniture in houses you have no access to. the shrug is the accurate answer and it has cost you two jobs.
cost: the whole distance for a few, the first inch for hundreds — few lives hold both, and there is no ledger either one could go in. the arrivals belong to the people who made them and the beginnings answer to names you never learned, so nothing that worked has ever come back round to you as work.

lead: the only object with your name on it took nine days and is free to anybody. the four hundred hours a year you spend walking people through the same thing have never been written down by anybody, including you.
sun: what you do cannot be shown to anybody — hours in a passenger seat and on the end of a phone, the stretch where somebody would have stopped, and none of it leaves an object behind. so the one document stands in for the whole competence. people find it, use it, get most of the way, and the ones who stall where everybody stalls write to you and get the actual article.
moon: the document carries your name at the top and nothing else — no letterhead, no terms, no line about what cannot be done with it. it turns up inside two firms' training packs, one of them with the name still on it. the same bareness that lets a stranger use it at midnight lets anybody put their own header on it.
pull: twenty years of walking leaves no object; nine days at a desk left one, and that is the part of you anybody can find.
tension: the paper is what your name means now. someone who needed the whole distance downloads it instead, gets to the place where everybody stops, and concludes they were not up to it — because the visible offer is nine days of typing and the real offer has no page. you cannot advertise the other thing. describing it accurately amounts to saying that the document is not enough, which is a sentence only somebody selling something says.
cost: instructions written by somebody who has taken forty people through assume nothing, which is why yours work at three in the morning for a stranger with nobody to ring. it went out with no cover on it and none has been added since — you were not thinking about strangers when you wrote it, and strangers are now the whole of what your name attaches to.

lead: your own household cannot account for your thursdays. eleven years of them, and what was happening on each was a road, a person you never brought home, and the last part of something being done with them.
sun: the work is done out of sight of everybody who knows you, because it happens on the way somewhere and the way somewhere is nowhere. you are not at the office, not at home, not at any of the addresses anybody has for you. the person beside you knows exactly where you are, and then arrives, and the only witness to your whereabouts walks off into a life you have no part in.
moon: you would tell anybody who asked, and the shape of the thing is that nobody asks, because there is no post you hold that would make your movements a matter for anybody. so the absences accumulate as a texture rather than a fact — away a lot, hard to catch, always just leaving — and the texture is what people have when they describe you.
pull: every person you delivered can be found at an address tonight. the eleven years that put them there happened in a place nobody who loves you could point to.
tension: the reading that gets made of somebody who is out one evening a week for eleven years and vague about it is not a kind one, and it was made in your house some years ago and never withdrawn. the account that would settle it needs witnesses, and the witnesses are people who moved to other towns and would say you gave them a lift. so it sits there, and you have stopped correcting it.
cost: the last stretch needs somebody free on a thursday for a year, and being attached to nothing is what makes you free that way; nobody has to be squared with, no arrangement gets disturbed. the same fact runs backwards through your own week. what you spent those years doing exists whole in people who have moved on, and nowhere in the record of where you were.

lead: the settlement went through on a wednesday and he was glad and that was the end of it for him. The Claws were closed on two things by then, and only one of them had anywhere to arrive.
sun: you are in it for the length of a fight — the meetings, the drafting, two years of it, all the way to the day it is over, and then the edge, and he walks into the rest of his life. that part is clean. you have done it six times, each ending with a handshake in a corridor and you going back to the car.
moon: the grip that went round his case went round the matter underneath it at the same time, and only one of those had a person attached who could finish. he finished. the other grip is shut. four years on you can recite what the other side did in the second year, to nobody, about a matter that concluded for everyone else on that wednesday.
pull: he arrived, and you turned round at the edge with one hand still closed on the half of it that was never going anywhere.
tension: you get called relentless, and it is meant as praise by the ones who hired you and as a warning by everybody else, and both are working from the same fact: the case is over and you are still in it. none of that reaches the second grip. you were only ever half in it on his account; the other half was the matter itself, which had no destination and therefore no place for you to stop.
cost: a fight run by somebody who cannot be exhausted out of it is a different fight, and the people who come to you have usually already been worn down by one. you take them the whole distance and they get to stop. stopping is the move the second grip has never had, so the thing you carried them out of is still, in your hands, going on.
